newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Patten welcomes Blair's visit to HK gala ceremony.
newsitem.headline: Patten welcomes Blair's visit to HK gala ceremony.

text.p: Hong Kong governor Chris Patten welcomed Wednesday's announcement by British Prime Minister Tony Blair that he would attend the ceremony marking Hong Kong's handover to China at midnight on June 30.
"I warmly welcome the Prime Minister's announcement that he is to visit Hong Kong on June 30 for the handover ceremonies," Patten said in a statement.

"It underlines the strong personal and political interest Mr Blair has consistently taken in Hong Kong and is a reflection of the importance Hong Kong continues to have in British foreign policy," the statement said.
Blair ended weeks of speculation when he told parliament that he would be attending the gala ceremony.

Blair, asked in the House of Commons whether Britain owed a moral duty to the people of Hong Kong which would not end with the handover ceremony, replied: "I do agree... I think that is important... I will be attending the ceremony myself."
The Labour government, swept to power in an election landslide on May 1, has said it will continue to put pressure on Beijing to respect human rights in Hong Kong after the colony's reversion.

The handover has been overshadowed by criticism from Britain and its Western allies of China's decision to set up an unelected legislature to replace Hong Kong's Legislative Council, returned by about one million voters in a 1995 poll.
The United States snubbed China on Tuesday by announcing that Secretary of State Madeleine Albright would boycott the investiture of the unelected legislature at the handover gala.

Speculation had been rife that Blair might shun the event altogether. The Foreign Office said earlier on Wednesday: "The government's position on the provisional legislature is well known. There has never been any question of British ministers attending the swearing-in of a provisional legislature chosen by a hand-picked body of 400."
